# Dharmik Vivek Shinde

> Backend & Systems Engineer · Music & Audio Enthusiast · Runner & Leader

Bengaluru & Chennai, India. B.Tech in Computer Science at VIT Chennai (expected May 2027, GPA 8.56/10). Schooling at Deeksha Center for Learning PU College, Bengaluru (92%).

Hi, I'm Dharmik. I like systems—getting into computers to understand how things work across Linux, backend engineering, cloud infrastructure, and networking. Most of what I know came from building projects, running servers, and solving problems I had no idea how to handle when I started. Outside of tech: music, running, lifting, timepieces, instruments.

Extremely social and collaborative — a leader and public speaker. Former school house captain. Member & former Chair of LUGVITC (Linux Users Group, VIT Chennai).

## Experience

- **HummingWave Technologies** — Full Stack Developer Intern, May 2026 – Jul 2026. Next.js BFF architecture, Figma implementation, AWS S3 dynamic asset storage, Flutter webview components.
- **LumiEther Research LLP** — Backend Engineering Intern, May 2025 – Jul 2025. Custom Java (Quarkus) JSON-schema workflow engine; WebSockets + REST multimedia processing stack.
- **Linux Users Group (LUGVITC)** — Former Member & Former Chairperson (member since Sept 2023; Chair Apr 2025 – Apr 2026). Led technical events and Cyber-0-Day CTFs; managed custom Linux VMs for 500+ participants.

## Projects

- **scooby** — home server infrastructure defined in code: Docker, Prometheus, Grafana, Cloudflare Tunnels. https://github.com/iamdmix/scooby
- **dotfiles** — dotfiles and keyboard-first setup for macOS. https://github.com/iamdmix/dotfiles
- Other open source: habit-tui (Go/Bubble Tea habit tracker), TerminalSix (CTF platform), chhaya (climate-tech). https://github.com/iamdmix

## Writing

Technical blog at https://blog.dharmikshinde.tech — practical systems writing, mostly Docker and Linux, written slowly from real experience. Recent pieces include "Ricing macOS Without Losing Your Mind", "Docker Engine Under the Hood", "Docker Compose, Networks & Volumes for Beginners", "Production Docker Builds: 1 GB to 15 MB", and "VMs vs. Containers: What's Actually Different".
